correctness.rationale: The theorem is proved for every integer m>=3 and all real r>=0 via exact convex chamber inequalities. At r>0 each chamber has a unique sorted coordinate representation, intersections among distinct chambers have precisely one center particle and thus reduce to a convex two-particle center-face polytope. The finite polyhedral nerve theorem and an explicit simplex-to-star reduction give a bipartite graph; the classification follows from independently enumerated feasible occupation vectors and connectivity. At r=0 the coordinatewise contraction of the star descends to its symmetric cube. At r=L/2 and r=L weak inequalities retain their degenerate but convex cells, so the endpoint conventions are justified. The standalone verifier tests exact combinatorial formulas at representative rational values for m=3..11; independent linear programming confirmed chamber and center-face feasibility for m=3..6, including thresholds. Neither finite check substitutes for the general proof.

originality.rationale: The 2013 Dover--Ozaydin general parametric-polytope theory supplies an effective decomposition and bounds the number of types for ordered particles, but its inspected statements do not present or imply the explicit three-unordered-particle equal-star ranks and sharp threshold classification. The published two-particle study by Deeley and the later two-particle metric-star persistence model are different particle-count problems. Unrestrained star-braid results determine only the smallest positive-separation regime, and do not force the larger-radius collapse and component separation. The earliest public mathematical source is arXiv:1301.5693 (2013-01-24).
residual_risks: The full 2011 Deeley thesis was inaccessible; a plausible but unverified exact example in it cannot be ruled out from the abstract.
No bounded semantic index or literature search establishes absolute uniqueness; there may be unindexed equivalent formulae.
The finite standalone arithmetic checker does not independently certify the topological nerve-equivalence argument; independent expert verification has not been performed.

value.rationale: The claim gives a natural complete stagewise homotopy classification for a uniform infinite family of three-robot thick-particle configurations. Two sharp packing thresholds, half-arm and whole-arm, produce explicit nontrivial decreases of the free fundamental-group rank, followed by a predictable choose(m,3)-component locked configuration phase and a maximal-packing cutoff. These consequences are not obtained merely by an unrestrained braid-group computation and directly quantify the topology changes motivating the parametric-polytope literature.
